rationale:
Decision: split into 7 children. Five reuse comparator-accepted declarations at their identical frozen types: testform_dense, norm_props, eval_mass_bound, weak_limit_mass_bound and dilation_ball. Two are new nodes: countable_tests (Lemma CT) and diagonal_limit (steps 6–7). Steps 0–5 apply the registered dependency Submission.dimred_tr_blowup_calculus, so they stay in this node's assembly; no child uses blowup_calculus.

Why split. The supplied proof has two layers.
(A) Facts about currents on ℝ^P that never mention blow-ups:
 - Lemma CT: the countable family CT1, the test-value bound CT2 and the ε-argument CT3;
 - lower semicontinuity of local mass along ConvergesWeakly on varying domains (steps 3, 4);
 - the dilation–ball identities (steps 1, 2);
 - the diagonal selection (steps 6, 7).
These are genuine reusable obligations. Four are already accepted in other branches with exactly the needed types, which removes the heaviest new work: the grid partition of unity and covector separability of CT1.
(B) The blow-up calculus of steps 0–5. It stays here because a child can depend only on siblings.
Lemma CT was its own child (countable_tests, same frozen type) in attempts 1–4 of the grandparent decomposition. Attempt 5 merged it into this node only to respect max_children = 12; this split restores it.

Mapping of the supplied proof.
- CT1 → testform_dense (dor_lmbs_testForm_countable_approx): a countable D ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) approximating each test form uniformly, with all supports in one compact set. Also norm_props (rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props) part (iii): |α| ≤ C₀‖α‖, which is CT1(c).
- CT2 → eval_mass_bound (cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn).
- CT3 and the statement of Lemma CT → countable_tests. R is now chosen so that the common compact support set lies in B_{R+1}(0).
- Steps 3–4 → weak_limit_mass_bound (idtp_convergesWeakly_massOn_le), used twice.
- Ball identities of steps 1–2 → dilation_ball (dtc_bc_cz_blowUp_eval_dilation_ball).
- Steps 6–7 → diagonal_limit, for an abstract double sequence A_{k,i} with A_{k,i} → Z_k as i → ∞ and Z_k ⇀ C.

Parent assembly. Lean-checked against stubs carrying the exact frozen types:

subproblems.title: A countable family of test forms, uniformly dense with common compact supports (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Then there is a countable set D ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n: C^∞ compactly supported n-forms on ℝ^P whose topological support lies in U) with the following property. For every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) there are a compact set K ⊆ U with tsupport ω ⊆ K and a sequence (ω_k)_{k∈ℕ} in D such that tsupport ω_k ⊆ K for every k, ω_k → ω uniformly on ℝ^P, and dω_k → dω uniformly on ℝ^P. Here d = exteriorDerivative, and uniform convergence of covector-valued maps is with respect to the operator norm of covectors (the norm of Covector (Euclid P) k).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → ∃ D : Set (TestFormOn U n), D.Countable ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, ∃ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn U n), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ U ∧ tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K ∧ (∀ k, ωs k ∈ D) ∧ (∀ k, tsupport (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K) ∧ TendstoUniformly (fun k x => (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) atTop ∧ TendstoUniformly (fun k x => exteriorDerivative (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) atTop
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dor_lmbs_testForm_countable_approx (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.slicing-a1.testform_dense-a1, candidate b7ecbda9150d7985c7094c40f6aebfb81c4ec24b), reused at its identical frozen type. It replaces the hand-made family of step CT1 of the parent proof: Lemma CT only needs a countable family that approximates every test form uniformly with all supports in one compact set. The proof below summarizes the accepted node's proof as implemented by its Lean candidate and its accepted children (frozen imports only; the second countability of C(K, F) is proved directly, step 3).
Notation: Λ^k := Covector (Euclid P) k with its operator norm, so dist(a, b) = ‖a − b‖; d = exteriorDerivative; B̄(0, r) is the closed ball.

1. Compact exhaustion of U. For i ∈ ℕ put K_i := B̄(0, i+1) ∩ ⋂_{y ∈ ℝ^P∖U} {x : 1/(i+1) ≤ dist(x, y)}.
 - K_i is compact: each {x : 1/(i+1) ≤ dist(x, y)} is closed, an intersection of closed sets is closed, and a closed subset of the compact ball B̄(0, i+1) is compact.
 - K_i ⊆ U: if x ∈ K_i and x ∉ U, then y := x is an index of the intersection, so 1/(i+1) ≤ dist(x, x) = 0, which is false.
 - Every compact C ⊆ U lies in some K_i. Since C is compact, U is open and C ⊆ U, there is δ > 0 whose open δ-thickening of C lies in U (IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open); hence dist(x, y) ≥ δ for x ∈ C and y ∉ U. C is bounded, say ‖x‖ ≤ R on C. Choose i with 1/(i+1) < δ and R ≤ i + 1. Then every x ∈ C lies in B̄(0, i+1) and satisfies 1/(i+1) < δ ≤ dist(x, y) for every y ∉ U, so C ⊆ K_i.
2. Finite dimension. For every k, Λ^k is finite-dimensional: α ↦ (α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(k−1)}))_{I : Fin k → Fin P}, with (e_j) the standard basis, is a linear map into the finite-dimensional space (Fin k → Fin P) → ℝ, and it is injective because an alternating multilinear map is determined by its values on tuples of basis vectors (Module.Basis.ext_alternating) and a continuous alternating map by its underlying alternating map. A finite-dimensional real normed space is proper, hence second countable. So F := Λⁿ × Λ^{n+1} is a second-countable metric space.
3. Second countability of C(K, F) for a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P (sup metric dist(f, g) = sup_{x∈K} dist(f(x), g(x))). It suffices (Metric.secondCountable_of_countable_discretization) to give, for every ε > 0, a map from C(K, F) to a countable set whose fibres have diameter ≤ ε.
 - Fix a dense sequence (s_l) in F and, for each y ∈ F, an index r(y) with dist(y, s_{r(y)}) < ε/4.
 - For each j ∈ ℕ fix a finite set t_j ⊆ K such that every x ∈ K has some p ∈ t_j with dist(x, p) < 1/(j+1) (K is compact).
 - Each f ∈ C(K, F) is uniformly continuous on the compact K; fix J(f) ∈ ℕ with dist(f(x), f(y)) < ε/4 whenever dist(x, y) < 1/(J(f)+1).
 - Code f by (J(f), (r(f(p)))_{p ∈ t_{J(f)}}) ∈ ℕ × List ℕ, a countable set. If f and g have the same code, put j := J(f) = J(g). For x ∈ K choose p ∈ t_j with dist(x, p) < 1/(j+1). Then r(f(p)) = r(g(p)) =: l, and dist(f(x), g(x)) ≤ dist(f(x), f(p)) + dist(f(p), s_l) + dist(s_l, g(p)) + dist(g(p), g(x)) < ε. Hence dist(f, g) ≤ ε.
4. One compact set. Fix a compact K and let X := {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ K}.
 - For ω ∈ X, ω and dω are continuous (dω is again a test form), and ω(x) = 0, dω(x) = 0 for x ∉ K, since tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ K.
 - Let Φ(ω) ∈ C(K, F) be x ↦ (ω(x), dω(x)). The subset Φ(X) of the second-countable space C(K, F) has a countable dense subset T ⊆ Φ(X). For t ∈ T choose σ(t) ∈ X with Φ(σ(t)) = t, and let D_K := σ(T). It is countable and every member has tsupport ⊆ K.
 - Let ω ∈ X and ε > 0. Pick t ∈ T with dist(Φ(ω), t) < ε and put η := σ(t). For x ∈ K, dist(ω(x), η(x)) and dist(dω(x), dη(x)) are at most dist(Φ(ω), Φ(η)) < ε (max metric on F). For x ∉ K all four values vanish. So both distances are < ε at every x ∈ ℝ^P.
5. The family. Let D := ⋃_i D_{K_i}, a countable union of countable sets, so countable.
6. Approximation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). tsupport ω is compact and contained in U, so tsupport ω ⊆ K_i for some i (step 1).
 - For each k choose ω_k ∈ D_{K_i} ⊆ D with dist(ω(x), ω_k(x)) < 1/(k+1) and dist(dω(x), dω_k(x)) < 1/(k+1) for all x (step 4).
 - Put K := K_i. Then K is compact, K ⊆ U, tsupport ω ⊆ K and tsupport ω_k ⊆ K for all k.
 - Given ε > 0, 1/(k+1) < ε for all large k, so ω_k → ω and dω_k → dω uniformly on ℝ^P (Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff). ∎
proof_key_steps: Compact exhaustion K_i of the open set U; every compact subset of U lies in some K_i.

Λⁿ and Λ^{n+1} are finite-dimensional (injective coefficient map), hence second countable; C(K, Λⁿ × Λ^{n+1}) is second countable for compact K by a countable discretization (finite nets, a dense sequence, uniform continuity).
For each K_i pull back a countable dense subset of {(ω, dω)|_{K_i} : tsupport ω ⊆ K_i}; forms and derivatives vanish off K_i.
D = ⋃_i D_{K_i}; given ω, take K_i ⊇ tsupport ω and ω_k ∈ D_{K_i} within 1/(k+1) of ω and dω everywhere.

subproblems.title: The Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors is a continuous seminorm dominated by the operator norm (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let F := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖), and let N := covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. N(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j) of ℝ^P. Then (i) N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α') for all α, α' ∈ F; (ii) N(t·α) = |t|·N(α) for all t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ F; (iii) there is a real C ≥ 0 with N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for all α ∈ F; and (iv) N : F → ℝ is continuous.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ α α' : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + α') ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm α') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ C * ‖α‖) ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.mass_eq_weight-a1.test_form_approx-a1.norm_props-a1, candidate f492ba4a003c8f1324077e050d48667ae23c7100), reused at its identical frozen type. Lemma CT uses part (iii), the coefficient bound |α| ≤ √(Pⁿ)·‖α‖ of step CT1(c) of the parent proof. The proof below summarizes the accepted node's proof as implemented by its Lean candidate.
Notation: e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j, so ‖e_j‖ = 1; 𝓙 is the finite type Fin n → Fin P; e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}).

1. Coefficient vector. For α ∈ F and I ∈ 𝓙 put c_I(α) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise, and let v(α) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙 have coordinates c_I(α). Since (if p then a else 0)² = (if p then a² else 0), the definition of N and EuclideanSpace.norm_eq give N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ (∗).
2. Linearity. Evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in α, so c_I(α + α') = c_I(α) + c_I(α') and c_I(t·α) = t·c_I(α) (both sides are 0 when I is not strictly increasing). Hence v(α + α') = v(α) + v(α') and v(t·α) = t·v(α).
3. (i). By (∗), step 2 and the triangle inequality in EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙: N(α + α') = ‖v(α) + v(α')‖ ≤ ‖v(α)‖ + ‖v(α')‖ = N(α) + N(α').
4. (ii). By (∗), step 2 and homogeneity of the norm: N(t·α) = ‖t·v(α)‖ = |t|·‖v(α)‖ = |t|·N(α).
5. Coordinate bound. For every I, |c_I(α)| ≤ ‖α‖: if I is strictly increasing, the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖; otherwise c_I(α) = 0.
6. (iii). Put C := √(#𝓙) ≥ 0. By step 5, Σ_I c_I(α)² ≤ #𝓙·‖α‖², so N(α) = √(Σ_I c_I(α)²) ≤ √(#𝓙·‖α‖²) = C·‖α‖.
7. (iv). By (i) and N(−β) = N(β), |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C·‖α − α'‖ by (iii). So N is Lipschitz with constant C, hence continuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: N(α) is the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector v(α) = (α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, else 0)_I, and v is linear.
(i) and (ii) are the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the Euclidean norm.
|α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖ gives N(α) ≤ √(card(Fin n → Fin P))·‖α‖, which is (iii).
|N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C‖α − α'‖, so N is Lipschitz and continuous, which is (iv).

subproblems.title: Evaluation bound |T(ω)| ≤ r·M_W(T) for tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω| ≤ r (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) and r ∈ ℝ. Write |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α and M_W(T) := T.massOn W ∈ [0, ∞]. By Simon 6.2.5, M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal T(φ) over φ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport φ ⊆ W and |φ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. If M_W(T) ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ r for every x ∈ ℝ^P, then |T(ω)| ≤ r·(M_W(T)).toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (r : ℝ), T.massOn W ≠ ∞ → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ r) → |T ω| ≤ r * (T.massOn W).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.eval_mass_bound-a1, candidate 7a706164baaf42fc7f55751247396a8836928310), reused at its identical frozen type. It is step CT2 of the parent proof ("mass controls test values"), with r in place of s. The proof below summarizes the accepted node's proof as implemented by its Lean candidate.

1. Homogeneity. For t ∈ ℝ and an n-covector α, (t•α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I) for every I : Fin n → Fin P, so Σ_I [I strictly increasing]((t•α)(e_I))² = t²·Σ_I [I strictly increasing](α(e_I))², and |t•α| = |t|·|α|. Also |α| ≥ 0, being a square root, and |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. r ≥ 0, because 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ r.
3. Put M := T.massOn W and m := M.toReal ≥ 0. Since M ≠ ∞, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ M implies a ≤ m for every real a (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal).
4. Admissible rescalings. Fix ε > 0 and let s := r + ε > 0. Let ω' := s⁻¹ • ω ∈ TestFormOn U n (a submodule). Then tsupport ω' ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, and by step 1, |ω'(x)| = s⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ r/s ≤ 1 for all x. Hence ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, and likewise −ω' (same tsupport, same pointwise norms).
5. Bound. By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ofReal(T ω') ≤ M and ofReal(T(−ω')) ≤ M. By step 3 and linearity of T, T ω' ≤ m and −T ω' = T(−ω') ≤ m, so |T ω'| ≤ m. Since T ω' = s⁻¹·T ω, |T ω| = s·|T ω'| ≤ (r + ε)·m.
6. Conclusion. ε > 0 is arbitrary and m ≥ 0, so |T ω| ≤ r·m = r·(T.massOn W).toReal. ∎
proof_key_steps: For ε > 0 both ±(r+ε)⁻¹ω are admissible for M_W(T).
le_massOn and M_W(T) ≠ ∞ give |T ω| ≤ (r+ε)·M_W(T).toReal; let ε → 0.

subproblems.title: Countable-test criterion: convergence on a fixed countable family plus local mass bounds gives weak convergence in ℝ^P (Lemma CT)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. There is a sequence (ω_m)_{m∈ℕ} in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) with the following property. Let V_k ⊆ ℝ^P (k ∈ ℕ) be arbitrary sets, A_k ∈ 𝒟_n(V_k) (GeometricCurrentOn (V_k) n) and A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Suppose that for every R ∈ ℕ there are k₀ ∈ ℕ and Γ ∈ [0, ∞) (Γ ≠ ∞) with M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A) ≤ Γ and, for every k ≥ k₀, B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ V_k and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A_k) ≤ Γ. Suppose also that currentEval(A_k, ω_m) → A(ω_m) as k → ∞ for every m. Then A_k ⇀ A in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly As A), i.e. currentEval(A_k, ω) → A(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Here B_r(0) is the open ball, M_W = massOn (the supremum of ofReal(T(φ)) over test forms φ of the current's domain with tsupport φ ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(φ(x)) ≤ 1 for all x), and currentEval(T, ω) = T(ω) if ω is a test form whose tsupport lies in the domain of T, and 0 otherwise.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, ∀ (Vs : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (As : (k : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Vs k) n) (A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ R : ℕ, ∃ (k₀ : ℕ) (Γ : ℝ≥0∞), Γ ≠ ∞ ∧ A.massOn (ball 0 ((R : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ Γ ∧ ∀ k, k₀ ≤ k → ball (0 : Euclid P) ((R : ℝ) + 1) ⊆ Vs k ∧ (As k).massOn (ball 0 ((R : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ Γ) → (∀ m, Tendsto (fun k => currentEval (As k) ((ωs m : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) atTop (𝓝 (A (ωs m)))) → ConvergesWeakly As A
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Step A (Lemma CT, criterion (C) of step 2(d) of the grandparent proof). The statement and the ε-argument are those of the supplied Lemma CT (its step CT3). The supplied step CT1 builds the countable family by hand (a smooth grid partition of unity times a dense sequence of covectors), and the supplied step CT2 bounds test values by mass. Both ingredients are taken here from comparator-accepted siblings with identical frozen types:
 - testform_dense = Submission.dor_lmbs_testForm_countable_approx supplies the countable family. It approximates every test form uniformly, with all supports in one compact set K. So the radius R below is chosen from K instead of from tsupport ω.
 - eval_mass_bound = Submission.cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn is CT2.
 - norm_props = Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props, part (iii), is the coefficient bound of CT1(c).
Notation: |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α and ‖α‖ := operator norm, for α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n; M_W := massOn; B := B_{R+1}(0) = ball 0 (R+1).

1. (The sequence.) Apply testform_dense with U := ℝ^P, which is open. It gives a countable set D ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with this property: for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) there are a compact K ⊇ tsupport ω and a sequence (ω'_j) in D with tsupport ω'_j ⊆ K for all j and ω'_j → ω uniformly on ℝ^P in the operator norm. The part about exterior derivatives is not used.
 - D is nonempty: applying the property to ω = 0 produces elements ω'_j ∈ D.
 - A countable nonempty set is the range of a sequence (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range). So D = {ω_m : m ∈ ℕ} for a sequence (ω_m) in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). This is the sequence of the statement.
2. (Norm comparison.) By norm_props (iii), fix C₀ ≥ 0 with |α| ≤ C₀·‖α‖ for every α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n.
3. Now let V_k, A_k and A satisfy the mass hypothesis (M) and the test hypothesis (T). Fix ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). We show currentEval(A_k, ω) → A(ω). Since ω is arbitrary, this is ConvergesWeakly (A_k) A.
4. (Choice of R, k₀ and Γ.) Take K and (ω'_j) from step 1 for this ω.
 - K is compact, hence bounded: K ⊆ B̄_r(0) for some r ∈ ℝ. Let R := ⌈r⌉₊ ∈ ℕ. Since r ≤ R < R + 1, K ⊆ B.
 - Take k₀ ∈ ℕ and Γ ∈ [0, ∞) from (M) for this R, and put G := Γ.toReal ≥ 0.
 - Then M_B(A) ≤ Γ < ∞, and for every k ≥ k₀, B ⊆ V_k and M_B(A_k) ≤ Γ < ∞. Hence M_B(A).toReal ≤ G and M_B(A_k).toReal ≤ G (ENNReal.toReal_mono).
5. (Choice of m.) Let ε > 0 and put η := ε/(4(C₀G + 1)) > 0. By uniform convergence choose j with ‖ω(p) − ω'_j(p)‖ < η for every p ∈ ℝ^P. Since ω'_j ∈ D, ω'_j = ω_m for some m.
6. (The difference form.) Let β := ω − ω_m.
 - tsupport β ⊆ tsupport ω ∪ tsupport ω_m ⊆ K ⊆ B.
 - For every p, |β(p)| ≤ C₀·‖ω(p) − ω_m(p)‖ ≤ C₀η, by step 2.
7. (Limit side.) β ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) and A is linear, so A(ω) − A(ω_m) = A(β). Apply eval_mass_bound with T := A, W := B, r := C₀η; it applies because M_B(A) ≠ ∞. It gives |A(ω) − A(ω_m)| ≤ C₀η·M_B(A).toReal ≤ C₀ηG.
8. (Sequence side.) Let k ≥ k₀.
 - tsupport ω and tsupport ω_m lie in B ⊆ V_k, so both forms are also test forms of the domain V_k. Write ω^♭, ω_m^♭ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V_k) for them.
 - By the definition of currentEval, currentEval(A_k, ω) = A_k(ω^♭) and currentEval(A_k, ω_m) = A_k(ω_m^♭).
 - By linearity of A_k, the difference is A_k(ω^♭ − ω_m^♭), and the underlying form of ω^♭ − ω_m^♭ is β.
 - Apply eval_mass_bound with T := A_k, W := B, r := C₀η; it applies because M_B(A_k) ≤ Γ < ∞. It gives |currentEval(A_k, ω) − currentEval(A_k, ω_m)| ≤ C₀η·M_B(A_k).toReal ≤ C₀ηG.
9. (Size of the error.) C₀ηG = ε·C₀G/(4(C₀G + 1)) ≤ ε/4, because C₀G ≥ 0.
10. (Tests.) By (T) for this m, there is k₁ with |currentEval(A_k, ω_m) − A(ω_m)| < ε/2 for every k ≥ k₁.
11. (Conclusion.) For k ≥ max(k₀, k₁), the triangle inequality and steps 7–10 give
 |currentEval(A_k, ω) − A(ω)| ≤ |currentEval(A_k, ω) − currentEval(A_k, ω_m)| + |currentEval(A_k, ω_m) − A(ω_m)| + |A(ω_m) − A(ω)| < ε/4 + ε/2 + ε/4 = ε.
 As ε > 0 was arbitrary, currentEval(A_k, ω) → A(ω). As ω was arbitrary, A_k ⇀ A in ℝ^P. ∎
Lean note (not part of the proof): this argument compiles in about 90 lines against stubs of the three siblings with their frozen types. It uses Set.Countable.exists_eq_range, IsCompact.isBounded.subset_closedBall, Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff, tsupport_sub, map_sub on the underlying linear map, and unfold currentEval followed by dite_eq_left (dif_pos is deprecated in this toolchain).
proof_key_steps: The accepted countable family D (testform_dense with U = ℝ^P) is nonempty and countable, hence the range of a sequence (ω_m).
Given ω, take the common compact support set K of its approximants and R ∈ ℕ with K ⊆ B_{R+1}(0); (M) gives k₀ and a finite bound Γ for A and for A_k, k ≥ k₀.
Pick ω_m uniformly η-close to ω; by norm_props (iii), β = ω − ω_m satisfies |β| ≤ C₀η and tsupport β ⊆ B_{R+1}(0).
eval_mass_bound gives |A(ω) − A(ω_m)| ≤ C₀ηG and, for k ≥ k₀, |currentEval(A_k, ω) − currentEval(A_k, ω_m)| ≤ C₀ηG ≤ ε/4.
With (T) for ω_m, |currentEval(A_k, ω) − A(ω)| < ε eventually; hence ConvergesWeakly.

subproblems.title: Diagonal selection: a diagonal of a double sequence of currents converges weakly to the iterated limit under uniform local mass bounds
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For k, i ∈ ℕ let V_{k,i} ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets and A_{k,i} ∈ 𝒟_n(V_{k,i}) (GeometricCurrentOn (V_{k,i}) n); for k ∈ ℕ let W_k ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets and Z_k ∈ 𝒟_n(W_k); let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P). Assume: (H1) for every k ∈ ℕ and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n), currentEval(A_{k,i}, ω) → currentEval(Z_k, ω) as i → ∞; (H2) Z_k ⇀ C in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly Zs C, i.e. currentEval(Z_k, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)); (H3) for every R ∈ ℕ there are k₀ ∈ ℕ and Γ ∈ [0, ∞) (Γ ≠ ∞) with M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(C) ≤ Γ such that, for every k ≥ k₀, for all sufficiently large i, B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ V_{k,i} and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A_{k,i}) ≤ Γ. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with A_{k,φ(k)} ⇀ C in ℝ^P, i.e. ConvergesWeakly (fun k ↦ A_{k,φ(k)}) C. Here B_r(0) is the open ball, M_W = massOn, and currentEval(T, ω) = T(ω) if ω is a test form whose tsupport lies in the domain of T, and 0 otherwise.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Vs : ℕ → ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (As : (k i : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Vs k i) n) (Ws : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Zs : (k : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Ws k) n) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ (k : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), Tendsto (fun i => currentEval (As k i) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) atTop (𝓝 (currentEval (Zs k) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)))) → ConvergesWeakly Zs C → (∀ R : ℕ, ∃ (k₀ : ℕ) (Γ : ℝ≥0∞), Γ ≠ ∞ ∧ C.massOn (ball 0 ((R : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ Γ ∧ ∀ k, k₀ ≤ k → ∀ᶠ i in atTop, ball (0 : Euclid P) ((R : ℝ) + 1) ⊆ Vs k i ∧ (As k i).massOn (ball 0 ((R : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ Γ) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ConvergesWeakly (fun k => As k (φ k)) C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 6 (diagonal selection) and step 7 (applying criterion (C)), stated for an abstract double sequence. In the parent, A_{k,i} = blowUp T (x_i + λ_i y) (λ_i s_k) and Z_k = blowUp S y s_k. There (H1) is step 5, (H2) is hypothesis (c), and (H3) comes from steps 1–4.
The supplied step 6 also demands λ_{i(k)} < 1/(k+1) and |x_{i(k)} − x| < 1/(k+1). Its only purpose is to obtain the domain and mass bounds of step 7(a). Here those bounds are written directly into the diagonal conditions, as clause (b) below, using (H3).
Uses the sibling countable_tests = Submission.dimred_tr_ibl_countable_tests.

1. Let (ω_m)_{m∈ℕ} be the sequence in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) given by countable_tests for (P, n).
2. Using (H3), choose for every R ∈ ℕ numbers k₀(R) ∈ ℕ and Γ(R) ∈ [0, ∞) with:
 - M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(C) ≤ Γ(R);
 - for every k ≥ k₀(R) and all sufficiently large i, B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ V_{k,i} and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A_{k,i}) ≤ Γ(R).
3. For k, i ∈ ℕ let Q(k, i) be the conjunction of:
 - (a) |currentEval(A_{k,i}, ω_m) − currentEval(Z_k, ω_m)| < 1/(k+1) for every m ≤ k;
 - (b) for every R ≤ k with k₀(R) ≤ k: B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ V_{k,i} and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(A_{k,i}) ≤ Γ(R).
4. For each fixed k, Q(k, i) holds for all sufficiently large i.
 - Clause (a), for one m ≤ k: (H1) with ω := ω_m gives currentEval(A_{k,i}, ω_m) → currentEval(Z_k, ω_m) as i → ∞. Since 1/(k+1) > 0, the inequality holds for all large i.
 - Clause (b), for one R ≤ k: if k₀(R) ≤ k it holds for all large i by step 2; if k₀(R) > k it holds vacuously.
 - Only finitely many m and R occur (m, R ∈ {0, …, k}). A finite intersection of sets of the form "for all large i" is again of that form (Filter.eventually_all_finite with the finite set {0, …, k}).
5. (Diagonal.) Apply the diagonal extraction lemma Filter.extraction_forall_of_eventually: if for every k the property Q(k, ·) holds for all large i, then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with Q(k, φ(k)) for every k. Fix such a φ and put D_k := A_{k,φ(k)} ∈ 𝒟_n(V_{k,φ(k)}).
6. (Mass hypothesis of countable_tests for D_k and C.) Let R ∈ ℕ, k₀' := max(k₀(R), R) and Γ := Γ(R) < ∞.
 - M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(C) ≤ Γ by step 2.
 - For k ≥ k₀' we have R ≤ k and k₀(R) ≤ k. So clause (b) of Q(k, φ(k)) gives B_{R+1}(0) ⊆ V_{k,φ(k)} and M_{B_{R+1}(0)}(D_k) ≤ Γ.
7. (Test hypothesis of countable_tests.) Fix m.
 - For k ≥ m, clause (a) of Q(k, φ(k)) gives |currentEval(D_k, ω_m) − currentEval(Z_k, ω_m)| < 1/(k+1). Since 1/(k+1) → 0, currentEval(D_k, ω_m) − currentEval(Z_k, ω_m) → 0 by squeezing.
 - By (H2) applied to ω_m ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), currentEval(Z_k, ω_m) → C(ω_m).
 - Adding the two limits gives currentEval(D_k, ω_m) → C(ω_m).
8. Apply countable_tests with V_k := V_{k,φ(k)}, A_k := D_k and A := C. Its hypotheses are steps 6 and 7. So D_k ⇀ C in ℝ^P, i.e. ConvergesWeakly (fun k ↦ A_{k,φ(k)}) C. Together with the strict monotonicity of φ, this proves the claim. ∎
Lean note (not part of the proof): this argument compiles in about 35 lines against a stub of countable_tests with its frozen type. It uses choose on (H3), Filter.Eventually.and, Filter.eventually_all_finite (Set.finite_Iic k), Filter.extraction_forall_of_eventually, squeeze_zero_norm' with tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat, and Tendsto.add.
proof_key_steps: Fix the countable test sequence (ω_m) of countable_tests and choose k₀(R), Γ(R) from (H3).
For each k, the finitely many conditions 'test values on ω_m within 1/(k+1) of those of Z_k for all m ≤ k' and 'domain and mass bounds for all R ≤ k with k₀(R) ≤ k' hold for all large i.
Filter.extraction_forall_of_eventually gives a strictly increasing φ satisfying all of them at i = φ(k).
Then D_k = A_{k,φ(k)} meets the mass hypothesis of countable_tests (k ≥ max(k₀(R), R)) and its test hypothesis (squeeze plus (H2)); so D_k ⇀ C.

subproblems.title: Mass bounds pass to ConvergesWeakly-limits of currents on varying domains (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, all sets U_j ⊆ ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) and V ⊆ ℝ^P, all currents T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U_j) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(V), every set W ⊆ ℝ^P and every B ∈ [0, ∞]: if T_j ⇀ S in the sense of ConvergesWeakly (currentEval(T_j, ω) → S(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V)) and, for all sufficiently large j, W ⊆ U_j and M_W(T_j) ≤ B, then M_W(S) ≤ B. Here M_W = massOn is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over test forms ω of the current's domain with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm ≤ 1 everywhere.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) n) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (B : ℝ≥0∞), ConvergesWeakly Ts S → (∀ᶠ j in atTop, W ⊆ Us j ∧ (Ts j).massOn W ≤ B) → S.massOn W ≤ B
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.idtp_convergesWeakly_massOn_le (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.integer_density_tangent_planes-a1.weak_limit_mass_bound-a1, candidate fb9bfaa2bb3b6a2fb2c8d2c902f098a63fc92f2d), reused at its identical frozen type. It is the argument used twice in steps 3–4 of the parent proof: "S(β) = lim_i currentEval(B_i, β) ≤ Γρⁿ; taking the supremum, M_{B_ρ(p)}(S) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ)", and the same for C. The proof below summarizes the accepted node's proof as implemented by its Lean candidate.

1. By definition M_W(S) = S.massOn W is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ofReal(S(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn V n W, i.e. over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for every x. So it suffices to fix such an ω and prove ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ B.
2. By hypothesis there is j₀ such that W ⊆ U_j and M_W(T_j) ≤ B for every j ≥ j₀. Let j ≥ j₀.
 - ω is a test form and tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ U_j. So the same form defines ω_j ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U_j), and currentEval(T_j, ω) = T_j(ω_j) by the definition of currentEval.
 - ω_j has the same support and the same pointwise coefficient norms as ω, so ω_j ∈ massAdmissibleOn U_j n W.
 - Hence ofReal(T_j(ω_j)) ≤ M_W(T_j) ≤ B (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Thus ofReal(currentEval(T_j, ω)) ≤ B for every j ≥ j₀.
3. By ConvergesWeakly, currentEval(T_j, ω) → S(ω), and ENNReal.ofReal is continuous, so ofReal(currentEval(T_j, ω)) → ofReal(S(ω)). The set {t ∈ [0, ∞] : t ≤ B} is closed and contains the terms with j ≥ j₀, hence the limit: ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ B.
4. Since ω was an arbitrary admissible form, M_W(S) ≤ B. ∎
proof_key_steps: M_W(S) is the supremum of ofReal(S(ω)) over admissible ω; fix one.
For j ≥ j₀, tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ U_j, so currentEval(T_j, ω) = T_j(ω) with ω admissible for M_W(T_j); hence ofReal(currentEval(T_j, ω)) ≤ B.
ConvergesWeakly and continuity of ofReal pass the bound to ofReal(S(ω)); take the supremum.

subproblems.title: The dilation η_{x,λ} maps B_ρ(x) onto B_{ρ/λ}(0) (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, x ∈ ℝ^P, ρ ∈ ℝ and λ > 0, and let η = η_{x,λ}, η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x) (Contract `dilation x λ`, y ↦ −λ⁻¹x + λ⁻¹y; ℝ^P = Euclid P). Then η⁻¹(B_{ρ/λ}(0)) = B_ρ(x) and η(B_ρ(x)) = B_{ρ/λ}(0), where B_r(a) = {y : ‖y − a‖ < r} is the open Euclidean ball (empty when r ≤ 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (x : Euclid P) (ρ lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → dilation x lam ⁻¹' ball 0 (ρ / lam) = ball x ρ ∧ dilation x lam '' ball x ρ = ball 0 (ρ / lam)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dtc_bc_cz_blowUp_eval_dilation_ball (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.blowup_compactness-a1.codim_zero-a1.blowup_eval-a1.dilation_ball-a1, candidate a5221e20d5f0bbbca1f0143f5d26620caab740b8), reused at its identical frozen type. It supplies the ball identities of steps 1 and 2 of the parent proof: dilation x″ t '' B_{δ′}(x″) = B_{δ′/t}(0), and dilation a t ⁻¹' B_ρ(0) = B_{tρ}(a), the latter by applying it with radius tρ. The proof below summarizes the accepted node's proof as implemented by its Lean candidate.

1. Formula. By the Contract definitions, η(y) = −(λ⁻¹x) + dilationCLM P λ y with dilationCLM P λ = λ⁻¹·id. So η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x) for every y. Since λ > 0, ‖η(y)‖ = λ⁻¹‖y − x‖.
2. Preimage. For y ∈ ℝ^P: y ∈ η⁻¹(B_{ρ/λ}(0)) ⟺ λ⁻¹‖y − x‖ < ρ/λ ⟺ ‖y − x‖ < ρ (multiply by λ > 0) ⟺ y ∈ B_ρ(x). Hence η⁻¹(B_{ρ/λ}(0)) = B_ρ(x). No sign condition on ρ is used.
3. Image, ⊆. If y ∈ B_ρ(x), then η(y) ∈ B_{ρ/λ}(0) by step 2. So η(B_ρ(x)) ⊆ B_{ρ/λ}(0).
4. Image, ⊇. Let z ∈ B_{ρ/λ}(0) and y := x + λz. By step 1, η(y) = λ⁻¹(λz) = z. Hence y ∈ η⁻¹(B_{ρ/λ}(0)) = B_ρ(x) by step 2, and z = η(y) ∈ η(B_ρ(x)).
5. Steps 2–4 give both identities. ∎
proof_key_steps: η(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x), so ‖η(y)‖ = λ⁻¹‖y − x‖ for λ > 0.
η(y) ∈ B_{ρ/λ}(0) ⟺ ‖y − x‖ < ρ, giving the preimage identity.
The image identity follows from the preimage identity and z = η(x + λz).
